collinearity occurs when wrote aor mote predictors are heavily correlated to each other, increases uncertainty in coefficient variables

can diagnose collinearity using Variance inflation facor
VIF over 5 indicates a problematic amound of colinearity
solutions: drop one of the collinear varibales with VIF>5 from the regression
combine collinear variables together into a single predictor.

VIF varianec inflation factor means how much the behaviour of a feature is influenced by it's relationship with other features. VIF is the coefficient estimate Bjhat/the variance of Bjhat
VIF gives a sense of how much a variable is contributing to the standard error in the regression.



```{r}
library(tigris)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

counties <- counties(state = "CA")
roads <- roads(state = "CA",
               county = "Santa Clara")
school_districts <- school_districts(state = "CA")
ca <- states() %>% 
  filter(NAME == "California")

ggplot(school_districts)+
  geom_sf(data = ca)+
  geom_sf()


```

```{r}
library(readr)
library(magrittr)
library(dplyr)
library(tigris)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

aqi22<-read_csv("aqi22_clean_ca.csv")
aqi22 %<>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X","Y"))

aqi22 %<>%
  st_set_crs(st_crs(school_districts))
aqi22 %<>%
  filter(`Pollutant Standard` == "PM25 24-hour 2012" & 
           `State Name` == "California")
school_districts %<>%
  st_join(aqi22)

school_districts %<>%
  group_by(GEOID)%>%
  summarise(mn_aqi = mean('Arithmetic Mean', na.rm = T)

ggplot(school_districts)+
  geom_sf(data = ca)+
  
            

  


```
